newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond new issues on hold for Fed watch.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond new issues on hold for Fed watch.

text.p: Corporate bond primary activity remained on hold Monday as many players observed a Jewish holy day and the market waited for the Federal Reserve to make its next move in U.S. monetary policy, dealers said.
"There's no calendar for new issues out there," said one syndicate source. "Things are on hold for now as players focus on Tuesday's Fed meeting."

The Fed's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy -setting arm meets Tuesday, September 24. Issuers are sidelined awaiting the FOMC's decision amid speculation that it will raise official U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
"Issuance is basically at a standstill as we approach tomorrow's (FOMC) meeting coupled with thinly staffed desks due to the holiday," one syndicate source said.
Some market players were out in observance of Yom Kippur, dealers said.
Looking ahead, Petronas is expected to price $500 million in debt via joint lead managers Salomon Brothers and CS First Boston, in the upcoming weeks.
In the government market, the 30-year bond is off 8/32 at 96-3/32 to yield 7.06 percent compared with 7.04 percent at Friday's close.
